$comment: Declarative desired state for the AI Studio Claude Code environment.
This file is DATA. bootstrap reads it to converge the machine; doctor reads it to
report drift. Neither hardcodes a capability list. Adding a capability means editing
this file, not editing code -- see docs/adding-a-capability.md.
Absolute machine paths NEVER appear here. Anything machine-specific is resolved at
runtime (see lib/detect.py) or supplied by the operator via environment variables.

studio.name: AI Studio
studio.$comment_minClaudeCode: 2.1.121 is the first release with MCP tool search + alwaysLoad.

prerequisites.name: Claude Code
prerequisites.install: Install the Claude Code VS Code extension or the standalone CLI from https://code.claude.com
prerequisites.notes: The VS Code extension ships its own binary that is not on PATH; detection searches for it.

prerequisites.name: Node.js (provides npx for stdio MCP servers)
Python 3.10+
prerequisites.notes: Runs the vault MCP servers (graphify.serve, aistudio-retrieval) and this CLI.

prerequisites.name: Google Chrome
prerequisites.notes: Required by chrome-devtools MCP for traces and Lighthouse.

prerequisites.name: typescript-language-server + typescript@5
prerequisites.notes: Pin typescript to ^5: the typescript-lsp plugin resolves typescript/lib/tsserver.js, which TypeScript 7 no longer ships at that path.

prerequisites.name: GitHub CLI
prerequisites.notes: Optional. GitHub capability is owned by the github MCP server; gh is a convenience fallback and an alternative credential source for the headers helper.

mcpServers.owns: Ad-hoc structural queries over the vault knowledge graph.
Deterministic retrieval over the vault: decisions, project state, precedent.
Browser evidence: screenshots, Lighthouse (perf + a11y), performance traces, console and network.
Driving a UI: clicks, forms, keyboard walks, accessibility-tree snapshots, responsive QA.
Component and section sourcing across shadcn and namespaced registries.
Design source of record: frames, Auto Layout, spacing, type, variables.

auth.operatorAction: Run /mcp in Claude Code, pick figma, choose Authenticate, complete the browser flow.
auth.notes: Read paths work on any seat. Write/generate paths need a Dev or Full seat.

mcpServers.owns: Remote GitHub: repositories, branches, commits, PRs, issues, Actions/CI status, releases, repository creation.

auth.operatorAction: Ensure a GitHub credential exists in the OS store: either 'gh auth login', or push once over HTTPS so Git Credential Manager stores one. Alternatively export GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.
auth.storedBy: OS credential store (Git Credential Manager or GitHub CLI). NEVER written to ~/.claude.json or this repository.
auth.notes: api.githubcopilot.com does not support RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, so Claude Code cannot OAuth against it. The headers helper reads a token at connect time instead, which keeps zero credentials at rest in configuration.

mcpServers.owns: Transactional email operations for the Adamenko site: domain + DNS verification status, delivery logs, suppressions, and sending a real test message. The application itself keeps its own Resend REST call — this server is for OPERATING and INSPECTING the account, not for delivering site mail.

auth.operatorAction: Run /mcp in Claude Code, pick resend, choose Authenticate, complete the browser login to Resend.
auth.notes: Resend-hosted remote server (official: github.com/resend/resend-mcp, npm resend-mcp, maintained by the Resend team). OAuth chosen over a Bearer API key so NO Resend key is ever written to configuration or this repository. A local stdio alternative exists (npx -y resend-mcp) but requires RESEND_API_KEY at rest, which this studio avoids.

mcpServers.owns: Generative visual media: image generation (to 4K), short video (to ~15s), character/style training (Soul), and browsing generation history. Fronts 30+ models (Soul, Cinema Studio, Flux, Seedream, Kling, Minimax Hailuo, Veo) behind one server, which is the reason to prefer it over wiring individual model vendors.

auth.operatorAction: Run /mcp in Claude Code, pick higgsfield, choose Authenticate, complete the browser login to Higgsfield.
auth.notes: Official Higgsfield-hosted remote server (higgsfield.ai/mcp). OAuth in-client, so NO API key or secret is written to configuration or this repository -- the same reason resend and figma are remote+OAuth here rather than local+key. Community stdio alternatives exist (geopopos/higgsfield_ai_mcp) but require HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY + HIGGSFIELD_SECRET at rest. Generation consumes Higgsfield plan credits.

mcpServers.owns: Google Search Console data: search-analytics performance (clicks, impressions, CTR, average position) by query, page, country, device and date; quick-wins detection; sitemap listing; URL/index inspection. The organic-search evidence layer -- what people actually searched to reach a site, as opposed to what we assume they searched.

auth.operatorAction: Create a service account in the Google Cloud project, download its JSON key OUTSIDE any repository, add the service-account email as a user on the Search Console property, then set GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS to the key path (Windows: setx GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS "C:\\path\\to\\key.json") and run: studio bootstrap
auth.storedBy: OS user environment holds the PATH; the key file lives outside every git repository. Neither the key nor its contents are ever written to ~/.claude.json or this repository.
auth.notes: Community server (npm mcp-server-gsc, MIT, ~251 stars, v0.3.0 published 2026-02-13 -- maintained but not fast-moving; Google publishes no official Search Console MCP). Verified 2026-07-27 by enumerating tools/list against live credentials: 8 tools -- list_sites, search_analytics, enhanced_search_analytics, detect_quick_wins, list_sitemaps, get_sitemap, index_inspect, and submit_sitemap. NOTE: submit_sitemap is a WRITE. The server is therefore NOT read-only by construction; read-only is enforced by granting the service account Search Console 'Restricted' permission (siteRestrictedUser), which cannot submit. Grant Restricted unless a task genuinely needs to write. The process EXITS with 'GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable is required' when the variable is absent, so it is gated the same way perplexity is. Access is scoped by Search Console user permissions, not IAM. If this server rots, the same data is one REST call away at searchconsole.googleapis.com.

mcpServers.owns: Searched, citation-bearing research against the live web: ranked search (perplexity_search), conversational search (perplexity_ask), multi-step deep research with sources (perplexity_research), and reasoning over retrieved material (perplexity_reason).

auth.operatorAction: Create a key at https://console.perplexity.ai, then set it as a USER environment variable named PERPLEXITY_API_KEY (Windows: setx PERPLEXITY_API_KEY "..."), reopen the terminal, and run: studio bootstrap
auth.storedBy: OS user environment. NEVER written to ~/.claude.json or this repository.
auth.notes: Official server (github.com/perplexityai/modelcontextprotocol, npm @perplexity-ai/mcp-server). No hosted HTTP/OAuth endpoint is documented, so an API key is the only supported auth. Verified 2026-07-27: the process EXITS with 'PERPLEXITY_API_KEY environment variable is required' when the variable is absent, so it is deliberately not written into ~/.claude.json until the key exists -- a configured-but-failing server degrades every session start. The stdio process inherits the OS environment, so no `env` block (and therefore no secret) is needed in configuration.

plugins.owns: Design DIRECTION for new UI: aesthetic point of view, type pairing, signature element.
Type-aware navigation and diagnostics in TS/JS repositories.
Specialised diff review agents: silent failures, type design, tests, comments.

skills.owns: Editorial finishing pass on final visitor-facing prose.
skills.$comment: Referenced upstream rather than vendored: actively maintained, installer is first-party, and pinning a copy would silently rot.

skills.owns: Design CRITIQUE of an interface that already exists: Scan, Diagnose, Fix.
skills.$comment: Vendored deliberately: the upstream repository ships 13 skills, only this one is wanted, and upstream is a fast-moving single-maintainer project. Review the diff before accepting any update. Provenance in the skill's PROVENANCE.md.

skills.owns: Building knowledge graphs from a corpus (/graphify).
skills.$comment: Installed by the graphify Python package itself (graphify claude install); not managed here.

config.owns: Capability routing: which capability fires when. The behavioural half of the system.
config.$comment: Written as a delimited managed block so operator-authored sections are preserved verbatim.

ownership.$comment: Explicit responsibility map. Overlapping ownership is a defect unless justified here.

git-local.scope: Local history: branches, commits, merges, rebases, worktrees, local tags.
git-local.notLocal: Anything touching a remote is GitHub, below.

github-remote.scope: Repositories, remote branches, PRs, issues, Actions/CI status, releases, repository creation.
github-remote.fallback: gh CLI, if installed. Not required, and deliberately not a second source of truth.

pr-review.owner: pr-review-toolkit agents (analysis) + github MCP (fetch and post)
pr-review.scope: Reading a diff and judging it. Agents analyse local changes; the MCP moves them to and from GitHub.
pr-review.note: Built-in /code-review and /security-review remain the general-purpose entry points.

ci-cd.scope: Workflow runs, job status, logs, re-runs.

vercel.note: Deliberately NOT integrated. Deploys are operator-owned; the Vercel MCP adds an OAuth wall for a workflow we do not automate.

research.owner: built-in WebSearch + WebFetch + the defuddle skill; perplexity MCP for searched, citation-bearing research
research.scope: External and current information: the web, current docs, competitor and reference material, anything outside training data.
research.note: Two tiers, and Claude picks. Built-ins answer a direct question or fetch a known page and are always available. The perplexity server adds ranked search and multi-step deep research that returns sources, which is what a claim needing citation wants. Neither is mandatory for any task; there is no rule that research must route through a vendor.

library-docs.scope: Version-accurate API surface for a named library, framework, SDK or CLI.
library-docs.note: Distinct from research: context7 answers 'what is the current API', WebSearch answers 'what exists in the world'. Prefer context7 for a named library because training data lags.

web-performance.owner: chrome-devtools MCP for real traces; AI-Studio tools/perf/psi.py for the PageSpeed Insights API; npx lighthouse for a keyless local lab run
web-performance.scope: How fast a live page actually is: Core Web Vitals, the LCP element and its phase breakdown, render-blocking and bandwidth contention, and CrUX field data where it exists.
web-performance.note: Three tools, different jobs, and picking wrong is how a session chases a score instead of fixing a page. chrome-devtools throttles the network and CPU FOR REAL -- use it for causation (which element is the LCP, which phase, did a change help). PSI and local Lighthouse SIMULATE throttling: reproducible, pessimistic, and genuinely noisy -- measured on one unchanged build, LCP ranged 3.2-4.1s across eight runs. Never conclude a change helped from one run before and one after. PSI's unique value is CrUX field data; when CrUX says none, the page lacks traffic and the lab number is the only signal, which is worth stating rather than hiding. PAGESPEED_API_KEY is optional (raises the quota); no key is needed for occasional use.

organic-search.owner: gsc MCP server (Search Console API; effectively read-only via a Restricted service account)
organic-search.scope: What people actually search to reach a site: queries, impressions, clicks, CTR, average position, by page/country/device/date. Plus sitemap submission state and index coverage.
organic-search.note: The only source of real query data -- rank trackers and keyword tools estimate, Search Console measures. Deliberately NOT paired with Google Analytics 4: this studio's sites run cookieless analytics (Vercel Web Analytics), and GA4 would force a consent banner for behavioural data that Search Console does not need. Traffic and Web Vitals are answered by Vercel Analytics; organic-search performance by this server. See the Adamenko google-infrastructure note for the reasoning.

local-search.owner: Google Places API (reviews, via the site's own sync script) -- Business Profile API pending operator application
local-search.scope: Local presence: reviews, and later Business Profile insights (discovery vs direct searches, calls, direction requests), posts and Q&A.
local-search.note: Google publishes no official Business Profile MCP, and the Business Profile API requires a formal access application plus a verified profile active 60+ days. Until that is granted, the working capability is the existing Places API key that already feeds the reviews pipeline. Do not add a second reviews path while that one works.

visual-assets.owner: shipped client imagery: the operator's real photography and verified institutional sources. Generated imagery and video: higgsfield MCP. Diagrams and vector work: code Claude writes (SVG, CSS, canvas).
visual-assets.scope: Imagery, illustration, motion and graphical assets, whether for exploration or for shipping.
visual-assets.note: The binding constraint is honesty, not the tool class: generated imagery is never presented as someone's real photography or as verified institutional data. Within that, generation is ordinary work -- concepting, mood and direction studies, placeholders, motion tests, internal presentation material. Higgsfield fronts 30+ models, so it is one integration rather than a per-vendor collection. Generation spends account credits, which is a reason to choose deliberately, not a rule against choosing.
